claude restart cli restored.nativeMetadata: The reference hands the failed continuation's items to its retry as a context handoff (delta_since_target_last_seen), which Rust does not build, and counts the handoff in the session's attachment budget.

claude delegate async.live: The reference records a delegated result inside the parent's running turn (the parent run's update comes before the subagent's completion records) and wakes the parent with a turn that opens with a checkpoint scope and the notification's message; Rust's delegation delivery records the completion first and starts the wake run without them.

claude delegate stop.live: Stopping the parent, the reference writes the interrupt request before the parent run's update and settles the stopped subagent after the turn ends; Rust's delegation writes the subagent and run updates first and settles the subagent before the turn's end.

claude delegate followup.live: The reference records a delegated result inside the parent's running turn (the parent run's update comes before the subagent's completion records) and wakes the parent with a turn that opens with a checkpoint scope and the notification's message; Rust's delegation delivery records the completion first and starts the wake run without them.
claude delegate followup.agent mcp: The reference issues the delegated child a new MCP credential for its follow-up turn (prepareMcpSession replaces a credential whose subagent lineage or access capabilities no longer match), and the new token changes its Claude query policy key, so it starts a CLI that resumes the child's session with its own mcp_set_servers. Rust keeps the child's credential and sends the follow-up to the CLI the child already runs. The reference does not replace the credential every run (it depends on timing), but does with CI's temporary directories.

codex thread tools.live: Racy: the pull-request syncs the thread tools start race the agent's next tool call (seen both matching, 1 of 8, and not): Rust reads a newly linked request right after its link, the reference through its sync reactor's queued sweep, so Rust's thread.pull-request-link-updated usually lands one link earlier.

claude delegate live.live: The reference delivers the delegated result into the parent's running turn and starts the parent's follow-up run within the same stream; Rust's delegation delivery starts no follow-up run there.

codex delegate live.live: The reference delivers the delegated result into the parent's running turn, writing the parent run's update before the subagent's completion and the notification item before the run's next update; Rust's delegation delivery writes them the other way round.
